Upload a tightly cropped product on a plain background; the cutout decides how clean the scene edges look.
Pick a preset scene first to see the lighting range, then replace it with a prompt or reference image.

A top-down shot pasted into an eye-level table scene reads as fake even when the lighting is right. Keep one master product photo per angle, and check label text and logo edges before the image reaches a listing.
Can a generated product shot be released without a photography QA pass?
Only for a rough concept. Product commerce still needs a pass for reflections, shadows and brand accuracy, because a clever AI render can still look wrong in a real storefront context.
Does a repeated prompt guarantee the same product angle or composition?
No. It can return a different framing, background or lighting even with the same object and prompt. Save the approved result instead of expecting prompt-level replication.
Not necessarily. Social, ecommerce and paid display often need different crops, compression and safe-zone treatment, so a single export is usually only one step of the asset process.
